The wrapper is `openmrsFetch` in `openmrs-esm-core`. The 401 coverage was added by commit `e16e2d9e` (PR #1754, "(test) Add regression tests for 401 Location-header redirect in openmrsFetch"). No ticket key is recorded for it.

**Why coverage was added:** The commit body is empty, so the reason is inferred from the title and test names, not stated by the author. The 401 branch can redirect to the server's `Location` header (an auth-module challenge such as `/module/authentication/login.form`) or fall back to the default login URL. Neither path had a test, so the commit adds one for each.

**What the new tests pin down** (all in `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-api/src/openmrs-fetch.test.ts`):
- A 401 with a `Location` header navigates to that header's URL, not the configured login page (lines 166-185).
- A 401 with no `Location` header navigates to the default `${openmrsSpaBase}/login` (lines 197-214).

The same commit also changes the existing 401 test's `// @ts-ignore` to `// @ts-expect-error`. It does not change any production code: the diff for `openmrs-fetch.ts` in that commit is empty.

**Relevant code:**
- The 401/403 branch picks the target as `redirectAuthFailure.url`, then the `Location` header, then `defaultRedirectAuthFailureUrl` (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-api/src/openmrs-fetch.ts:234`). It navigates there and either resolves or stays pending, depending on `resolvePromise` (lines 226-243).
- The 2xx session-endpoint `Location` redirect is separate (lines 187-195). Commit `9dae818f` added it under O3-5767. That ticket covers the 2xx path, not the 401 path the tests cover.
- Commit `a624af22` (PR #1918, "Support authentication failures from the backend") added the `rejectAuthFailure` option (`openmrs-fetch.ts`, around lines 237-242 and 287-291). I did not confirm whether its test (`openmrs-fetch.test.ts:235-243`) came from that PR or from elsewhere.

I could not read PR #1754's description, so if the ticket is recorded only there, I have not seen it.
